subject: P2: sudden throughput degradation — KV cache policy/hol blocking suspected
messages:
From: Simon Lewis <simon.lewis@acme-robotics.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-04T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — urgent

Rishi / Marissa,

We started seeing a large throughput degradation around 07:45 PDT — p95/p99 latency for our inference routes doubled and a subset of requests returned 502/504. Attaching recent logs and a small sample of failing request IDs (in acme_error_samples.zip).

Metrics snapshot:
- Normal qps: ~480 -> observed ~120 (sustained)
- p99 generation latency: 320ms -> 1100ms
- Error rate: 0.6% -> 5.9% (5xx from model runtime)

We haven't changed workload. The failure pattern looks like batches stuck and then a flood of evictions in your KV cache leading to hot request backpressure. Can you confirm if any KV policy or rollout ran in that window? We need ETA and whether to failover to smaller instances / alternate region. Customers are starting to escalate internally.

Simon
Head of Platform, Acme Robotics

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-04T08:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — urgent

Preliminary findings after 25m:
- We see a correlated spike of KV cache evictions that started at 07:44:38 PDT across the customer's dedicated pool. Eviction rate increased ~7x for a short window.
- The pattern is consistent with HOL (head-of-line) blocking: long-running large-seq requests are occupying the worker thread, preventing smaller prefix hits from using the cached KV, causing downstream batches to grow and then the runtime to trigger mass cache churn.
- There's evidence a config rollout completed 07:43:00 (kv-config.yml attached) that tightened max_cached_shards and enabled aggressive auto-evict on low-usage keys. That aligns with the timing.
- Model-level throughput counters show frequent batch size spikes (temporary coalesced batches of 16->64) which exacerbate backlog.

Short-term mitigations (we can apply immediately, estimated 8–12m to roll):
1) Revert the recent kv policy change (restore max_cached_shards to previous value).
2) Lower max_batch_size for the customer's route to 8 to reduce HOL risk.
3) Enable KV warming for hot prefixes and pin known hot keys (if they provide top prefixes).
4) Temporarily route overflow to a warm standby variant without the aggressive eviction policy.

I will run the revert in the canary pool then the dedicated pool if metrics improve. Attaching kv-config.yml and timeline chart.

-Hannah
SRE, Redwood Inference

From: Sean Gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>
Cc: Tessa Morgan <tessa_morgan@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-04-04T08:51:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — urgent

I started the canary revert at 08:48. Early telemetry: eviction rate dropping in the canary nodes; p95 latency improving ~25% on canary traffic. Plan to promote across the dedicated pool in waves (5m waves) and also push a runtime knob that caps batching for the customer's route.

Temporary mitigations I will do now (08:52):
- Set route override: max_batch_size=8, batching_window_ms=15
- Disable aggressive_auto_evict=true
- Add a KV pin list for the top-50 prefixes (hannah: please share if Acme can provide)

If these reduce p99 and error rate we'll keep for 24–48h and then explore a less blunt long-term change (adaptive eviction thresholds + hotkey detection).

-Sean
Principal Engineer, Serving Runtime

Date: 2026-04-04T09:10:00-07:00
Subject: Escalation: ACME-3472 — need exec approval for SLA credit / capacity burst

Tessa / Platform leadership — heads up: ACME (large customer) saw a production P2 caused by a config rollout that tightened KV cache policies and unintentionally triggered HOL blocking + cache thrash. SREs have applied a canary revert and route overrides; early metrics look better but the customer is asking for a credit and a short capacity burst to stabilize their steady-state traffic while we run a root-cause patch.

Summary:
- Impact window: 07:44 — 08:58 PDT (best-effort)
- Error spike to ~6%, p99 up to 1100ms, throughput down ~75% briefly
- Root cause: KV eviction policy change + workload with mixed long small sequences -> HOL blocking and spillback

Request:
- Approve one week of excess capacity (reserved nodes) for Acme to avoid repeated incidents while we push a safety gating change to rollout pipeline. Cost exposure estimate: ~$6k for the week.
- Approve a 10% service credit against April usage as a goodwill gesture (Marissa can confirm wording).

We need a quick yes/no. Will proceed with the mitigations regardless.

-rishi

Date: 2026-04-05T17:23:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production latency / 5xx spike — postmortem & next steps

Simon — thanks again for the samples and patience. We completed the canary revert and route override; metrics remained stable through the afternoon and we've kept the conservative batching config in place for 48h while we complete a deploy to add safety-gates to the KV-policy rollout.

Next steps:
- We will provide a short written postmortem by EOD tomorrow that includes the timeline, root cause, and permanent mitigations.
- We propose a temporary capacity buffer (one week) while we roll the fix; Rishi will follow up on the credit.
- If you can share the top prefixes for warm-pinning, Hannah can pre-populate KV to accelerate warmup.

We're very sorry for the outage and appreciate the partnership.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
